paper.title: Matroid Bandits: Fast Combinatorial Optimization with Learning

unmapped: feasible actions are the independent sets (bases) of a known matroid with L items and rank K
item weight vector drawn i.i.d. from arbitrary unknown distribution P on [0,1]^L (items may be correlated)
settings.definition_quote: A matroid bandit is a pair (M, P), where M is a matroid and P is a probability distribution over the weights w of items E in M... A subset of arms A \subseteq E can be pulled if and only if A is an independent set... After the arms A are pulled, we observe the weight of each item in A... we assume that the support of P is a bounded subset of [0, 1]^L.

unmapped: partition matroid of rank K over L items: equivalent to K independent Bernoulli bandits
settings.definition_quote: Let E be a set of L items and B_1, ..., B_K be a partition of this set... Let the weight of item e be drawn i.i.d. from a Bernoulli distribution with mean 0.5 if e = min_{i in B_k} i, 0.5 - Delta otherwise.

symbols.Delta_e_min: Delta_{e,K_e}: smallest positive gap between suboptimal item e and an optimal item with higher mean
symbols.G_e: sum_{k=1}^{K_e} Delta_{e,k}: sum of positive gaps of suboptimal item e to optimal items
symbols.sum_subopt: sum over suboptimal items e in E - A*

source.label: thm:gap-dependent
source.quote: The expected cumulative regret of OMM is bounded as: R(n) \leq \sum_{e \in \bar{A}^\ast} \frac{16}{\Delta_{e, K_e}} \log n + \sum_{e \in \bar{A}^\ast} \sum_{k = 1}^{K_e} \Delta_{e, k} \frac{4}{3} \pi^2.

results.notes: Regret defined w.r.t. fixed A* in expectation, i.e. pseudo-regret. Algorithm uses log(t), not n, so anytime. Sums are over suboptimal items (base arms) of the matroid; gaps defined relative to optimal items.

symbols.L_items: number of items L in the ground set of the matroid
symbols.m: rank K of the matroid (size of each basis)

source.label: thm:gap-free
source.quote: The expected cumulative regret of OMM is bounded as: R(n) \leq 8 \sqrt{K L n \log n} + \frac{4}{3} \pi^2 K L.

results.notes: Paper's K (matroid rank) mapped to m; paper's L (number of items) declared L_items.

symbols.L_items: number of items L in the ground set
symbols.m: rank K of the partition matroid (number of partitions)

conditions: partition matroid instance with optimal item mean 0.5 and all other items mean 0.5 - Delta in each partition

source.label: thm:lower bound
source.quote: For any partition matroid bandit \tilde{B} that is defined in Equations ... and parameterized by L, K, and 0 < \Delta < 0.5; the regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded from below as: \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{R(n)}{\log n} \geq \frac{L - K}{4 \Delta}.

results.notes: Consistent: E[T_e(n)] = o(n^alpha) for all alpha > 0 on every matroid bandit. Proof applies Lai-Robbins (via Bubeck & Cesa-Bianchi Thm 2.2) per partition.
